title: Continuous relation kernels on profinite bases in the finite-model derived hull
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $P$ be an extremally disconnected profinite space: $P$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected and the closure of every open subset is open. Give $\operatorname{Prof}/P$ the site of profinite spaces over $P$ with finite jointly surjective covering families, and let $q_P$ be its slice projection to the condensed topos [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site]. Put $R=q_P^*\Lambda$ and use ordinary internal $R$-modules and their ordinary uncompleted derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a finitely presented scalar $\Lambda$-module $B$, meaning a cokernel of a map of finite free scalar modules, put $B_R=R\otimes_{\underline\Lambda}\underline B$, with discrete constant underlines. A finite scalar local model on this site means an $R$-module which on a covering family has this form, with the scalar module allowed to vary [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Let $\mathcal H_P$ be the intersection of all full replete classes in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$ which contain $F[0]$ for every finite scalar local model $F$ on $\operatorname{Prof}/P$, and satisfy the following conditions. They contain zero and are closed under isomorphisms, all integer shifts, distinguished-triangle extensions, and retracts [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. A retract of $K$ is given by maps $K\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{p}K$ with $pi=1_K$. They are closed under all small products in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-category-product]. If $I$ is a small filtered category and $C_i^\bullet$ is a strict diagram of module-sheaf complexes with a common termwise lower bound, and all $Q(C_i^\bullet)$ belong to the class, then $Q(\varinjlim_i C_i^\bullet)$ belongs to the class. Here the colimit is termwise in module sheaves and $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For all finitely presented scalar modules $B,C$ and every actual $R$-module-sheaf morphism $v:B_R\to C_R$, the abelian sheaf kernel satisfies
$$ (\ker v)[0]\in\mathcal H_P. $$
The morphism need not come from a scalar map $B\to C$; for free $B,C$ its entries may be arbitrary continuous $\Lambda$-valued functions on $P$. No constant-rank, locally constant elementary-divisor, completeness, finite-field-valuedness, or finite-scalar-model assertion about the kernel is made. The empty space, zero scalar modules, zero rings, zero maps and identity maps are included.

source.place: Agent-formulated relation-kernel generation obligation on an extremally disconnected profinite base. HRS Example 3.1, Examples 3.6 and 4.2 and Section 4.1 specify the continuous-function coefficient category and the obstruction to replacing this assertion by finite-model kernel closure. Exact reference WANTED.

proof.text: First take finite $\Lambda=A$. Choose finite scalar generators of $B$. Their images under $v$ are continuous maps $P\to C$, hence locally constant, since $B,C$ are finite discrete. A common finite clopen partition makes all images constant. Scalar linearity and the generators then make $v$ the same scalar linear map on each part, on every profinite test. Its kernel there is the constant model of a finite $A$-module, hence finitely presented (choose finitely many generators and relations in a finite module over a finite ring). Consequently $\ker v$ itself is a finite scalar local model and its degree-zero complex is a generator. This also treats the zero ring.

source.place: Agent assembly; Example 3.1, Remark 3.2 and proof of Theorem 6.12(2).

proof.text: Now let $\Lambda=O=\mathcal O_E$; $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is the case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Apply integral scalar realization to $B,C,v$. Write $v_k$ for its maps on $B/\pi^kB,C/\pi^kC$ and $N_k=\ker v_k$. The entries of these finite maps are locally constant. Partition $P$ into finitely many clopens on which $v_k$ is a fixed finite scalar map. On each part $N_k$ is a finite scalar $O$-module killed by $\pi^k$; integral realization identifies its continuous-section sheaf with its scalar model. Thus $N_k$ is a finite scalar local model and $N_k[0]\in\mathcal H_P$. The actual quotient transitions give a strict tower $N_{k+1}\to N_k$. Integral realization identifies $\ker v=\varprojlim_kN_k$ as sheaves, without any claim that these transitions are surjective or uniformly stabilize.

source.place: Agent assembly; Example 3.1, Remark 3.2 and proof of Theorem 6.12(2).

proof.text: Apply finite-bundle Roos exactness to this tower, using $T=O$. Its hypotheses hold because every $N_k$ is the finite locally constant kernel bundle just constructed and every transition is induced by coefficient reduction. The distinguished triangle has first term $(\ker v)[0]$ and the other two terms $\prod_k^DN_k[0]$. Product closure, shifts and triangle extension closure put its first term in $\mathcal H_P$. This uses compact finite solution bundles, not a uniform stabilization of reduction images.

source.place: Agent assembly; Example 3.1, Remark 3.2 and proof of Theorem 6.12(2).

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$ (including $\mathbf Q_\ell$), finite scalar presentations give finite-dimensional scalar spaces. Choose bases $B\cong E^m,C\cong E^n$. Scalar extension carries these bases to free sheaf bases; the free-matrix correspondence expresses the actual sheaf map $v$ by one matrix $F$ with entries in $R(P)=C(P,E)$. These are the images of the basis sections at the terminal object, so the same matrix acts after every profinite base change. In particular the matrix is not replaced by a locally constant one.

source.place: Agent assembly; Example 3.1, Remark 3.2 and proof of Theorem 6.12(2).

proof.text: Apply Stonean continuous diagonalization to $F$, and write $D=LFU$ with diagonal entries $d_i$. The invertible continuous matrices give inverse sheaf isomorphisms by the same free-matrix correspondence. Multiplication by $U$ identifies $\ker D$ with $\ker F$. Sectionwise the diagonal equations are independent, so $\ker D\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^{\min(m,n)}K_{d_i}\oplus R^{m-\min(m,n)}$. The rank-one annihilator lemma applies to each $d_i$ and $\mathcal J=\mathcal H_P$, since all its generators and all its closure conditions are exactly among those defining $\mathcal H_P$. Each $K_{d_i}[0]$ therefore belongs to $\mathcal H_P$. The free remaining term is a generator. Finite sums are split-triangle extensions, so the displayed decomposition and repleteness prove the field case. All five permitted coefficients are covered. Empty bases and zero modules give empty matrices and empty sums; zero and identity maps give respectively the source generator and zero.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NC-a048be34b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four new nodes, the cited free-matrix, coefficient-extension, component-site and constructible nodes, the citer supported-image-bounded-derived-generation, and the sources: HRS Example 3.1, Remark 3.2, Lemma 4.1, Example 4.2 and Remark 6.4, Lemma 6.10 and Theorem 6.12; RTW Lemma 1.2.7 and Remark 2.3.5. The base proof was empty, so this is not a re-split order. Steps: step 1 (finite A, clopen-constant kernel) is elementary and correct. Step 2: integral realization is true (C(Q,O) tensor B = C(Q,B), Hom from B_R = Hom_O(B, C(P,C)) because P is final, ker v = lim ker v_k). Step 3: finite-bundle Roos is true for any profinite P (products exact via the Stonean basis; the solution space is a profinite cover with nonempty fibres by compactness, matching RTW 1.2.7); rotation, product and extension closure give ker v in H_P. Step 4: the free-matrix tool gives R^m to R^n as matrices over C(P,E); tool_use accepted. Step 5: Stonean diagonalization is true. I re-proved it: the max-pivot loci are open, their closures clopen, the bounded quotients extend by graph closure and Stonean projectivity, then induction on clopen pieces. The kernel decomposes as the sum of K_{d_i} plus R^{m-min}. Edge cases (m or n = 0, empty P, zero and identity maps) checked. No duplicates: local-smith needs locally constant type, field elimination needs constant rank, integers-profinite-tower covers only the ring. The rank-one field annihilator node is equivalent to the item's 1x1 field case and is reached by a genuine reduction, so D1/D2 do not apply. Its truth is OPEN: on HRS beta-N, K = H^0(fib(R -> prod e_n R)), and K in H_P is equivalent to the bounded-families module, and to coker(R -> R[1/f]), lying in H_P. I found neither a proof nor an obstruction (global sections kill K; the counit invariant used in the NN 8712600d and NY 03d9ef94 refutations is not known to survive products). Flag for L/human: this is the open core of the item, which already asserted it with reference WANTED.
